steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper on solving the Chinese Postman Problem with load-dependent costs using deep reinforcement learning with graph attention, plus new metaheuristics; motivate learning-based methods for routing and list our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:

- Machine learning / DRL as data-driven alternative; prior DRL work on TSP and VRPs
- Our focus: arc routing, CPP-LC, and why it is hard
- Contributions

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Routing problems are one of the core NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems and they play a crucial role in computer science and operations research (OR). There are many real-world applications of these problems in industries like transportation, supply chain, and operations management. Because of this they have attracted intensive research from the OR community, and various exact and heuristic approaches have been proposed. Exact methods are often limited by high time complexity, which makes them hard to apply to practical situations with large-sized instances. Heuristic methods, on the other hand, have traditionally been used a lot in real-world applications since they have lower computational time and complexity. But designing a heuristic algorithm is extremely difficult because it needs specific domain knowledge in both the problem and the implementation, and this is a significant challenge for algorithm designers when there are diverse combinatorial optimization problems in real-world applications. Also, heuristic algorithms solve problems by trial-and-error iterative procedures, which can take a lot of time, especially for large-scale problem instances. So it is essential and necessary to construct efficient data-driven methods for solving combinatorial optimization problems.

Recently machine learning methods (especially deep learning and reinforcement learning) have achieved outstanding performances in many applications in computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, etc. These data-driven methods also give an alternative way to solve combinatorial optimization problems, by automatically learning complex patterns, heuristics, or policies from generated instances, and this reduces the need for well-designed human rules. Machine learning-based methods can also speed up the solving process and reduce computation time with parallel hardware platforms like GPUs, which traditional algorithms cannot take advantage of. Some research has actually applied deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to routing problems, including Traveling Salesman Problems (TSP) and Vehicle Routing Problems (VRPs). But TSP and VRPs are simple node routing, while many real-world routing problems are defined on edges, i.e., arc routing, and solving them is more complex with numerous constraints.

  - applications: waste collection, mail delivery, bus routing
  - NP-hard; first arc routing problem where edge cost depends on length + vehicle weight (curb weight plus load)
  - harder solution space than TSP/VRP; exact methods only small instances; VNS, ILS simple
  - we propose three methods

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Routing problems are one of the core NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems and they play a crucial role in computer science and operations research (OR). There are many real-world applications of these problems in industries like transportation, supply chain, and operations management. Because of this they have attracted intensive research from the OR community, and various exact and heuristic approaches have been proposed. Exact methods are often limited by high time complexity, which makes them hard to apply to practical situations with large-sized instances. Heuristic methods, on the other hand, have traditionally been used a lot in real-world applications since they have lower computational time and complexity. But designing a heuristic algorithm is extremely difficult because it needs specific domain knowledge in both the problem and the implementation, and this is a significant challenge for algorithm designers when there are diverse combinatorial optimization problems in real-world applications. Also, heuristic algorithms solve problems by trial-and-error iterative procedures, which can take a lot of time, especially for large-scale problem instances. So it is essential and necessary to construct efficient data-driven methods for solving combinatorial optimization problems.

Recently machine learning methods (especially deep learning and reinforcement learning) have achieved outstanding performances in many applications in computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, etc. These data-driven methods also give an alternative way to solve combinatorial optimization problems, by automatically learning complex patterns, heuristics, or policies from generated instances, and this reduces the need for well-designed human rules. Machine learning-based methods can also speed up the solving process and reduce computation time with parallel hardware platforms like GPUs, which traditional algorithms cannot take advantage of. Some research has actually applied deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to routing problems, including Traveling Salesman Problems (TSP) and Vehicle Routing Problems (VRPs). But TSP and VRPs are simple node routing, while many real-world routing problems are defined on edges, i.e., arc routing, and solving them is more complex with numerous constraints.

In this paper we focus on the arc routing problem, specifically the Chinese Postman Problem with load-dependent costs (CPP-LC). It is a complex routing problem with various practical applications in waste collection, mail delivery, and bus routing. The CPP-LC is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem. It is the first arc routing problem where the cost of traversing an edge depends not only on its length but also on the weight of the vehicle (curb weight plus load) when it is traversed. The solution space of the CPP-LC can be much more irregular and challenging than for TSP and VRP. Exact methods for this problem need significant computational time and complexity, so they are only suitable for small instances. For larger instances some conventional heuristic approaches like Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS) and Iterated Local Search (ILS) have been applied, but they are still relatively simple and their solutions need substantial improvement compared to the optimal solutions. Because of these limitations we propose three methods to tackle CPP-LC effectively and improve on existing approaches in both computational time and solution quality. Our main contributions are:

- First, we model the CPP-LC problem as a sequential solution construction problem by defining a Markov decision process model for the arc routing problem, called Arc-MDP. This Arc-MDP model can be easily modified and applied to other arc routing problems and solved with DRL methods.

- Second, we present a new data-driven method based on Deep Reinforcement Learning and Graph Attention to solve this problem effectively and efficiently. The model can generate solutions for an instance in much less time than heuristic and exact methods.

- Last, we introduce two metaheuristic methods inspired by nature evolution and swarm intelligence, the Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), as new metaheuristics for CPP-LC. Then we conducted extensive experiments to compare our Arc-DRL with several heuristic baselines on various problem instances. The results show that our approaches perform better than previous methods in both solution quality and evaluation time.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Routing problems are among the core NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems and play a crucial role in computer science and operations research (OR). These problems have numerous real-world applications in industries such as transportation, supply chain, and operations management. As a result, they have attracted intensive research efforts from the OR community, and various exact and heuristic approaches have been proposed. Exact methods often face limitations in terms of high time complexity, which makes them difficult to apply to practical situations with large-sized instances. On the other hand, heuristic methods have traditionally been commonly used in real-world applications because of their lower computational time and complexity. However, designing a heuristic algorithm is extremely difficult because it requires specific domain knowledge in both the problem and implementation, which poses significant challenges for algorithm designers dealing with diverse combinatorial optimization problems in real-world applications. Moreover, heuristic algorithms solve problems through trial-and-error iterative procedures, which can be time-consuming, especially for large-scale problem instances. Hence, constructing efficient data-driven methods to solve combinatorial optimization problems is essential and necessary.

Recently, machine learning methods (especially deep learning and reinforcement learning) have achieved outstanding performances in various applications in computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, etc. These data-driven methods also provide an alternative approach to solving combinatorial optimization problems by automatically learning complex patterns, heuristics, or policies from generated instances, thereby reducing the need for well-designed human rules. Furthermore, machine learning-based methods can accelerate the solving process and reduce computation time with parallel hardware platforms like GPUs, which traditional algorithms cannot take advantage of. In fact, some research has applied deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to solve routing problems, including Traveling Salesman Problems (TSP) [1] [2] [3] and Vehicle Routing Problems (VRPs) [4] [5] [6] [7] [8]. However, TSP and VRPs are simple node routing, while many real-world routing problems are defined on edges, i.e., arc routing, and their solution is more complex with numerous constraints.

In this paper, we focus on the arc routing problem, specifically the Chinese Postman Problem with load-dependent costs (CPP-LC) [9], a complex routing problem with various practical applications in waste collection, mail delivery, and bus routing [10]. The CPP-LC is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem and is the first arc routing problem in which the cost of traversing an edge depends not only on its length but also on the weight of the vehicle (including curb weight plus load) when it is traversed. Compared to TSP and VRP, the solution space of the CPP-LC can be much more irregular and challenging. Exact methods for this problem require significant computational time and complexity and are only suitable for small instances. For larger instances, conventional heuristic approaches such as Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS) and Iterated Local Search (ILS) [9] have been applied, but they are still relatively simple, and their solutions need substantial improvement compared to the optimal solutions. Due to these limitations, we propose three methods to effectively tackle CPP-LC and improve on existing approaches in terms of both computational time and solution quality. Specifically, our main contributions are as follows:

- • Firstly, we model the CPP-LC problem as a sequential solution construction problem by defining the Markov decision process model for the arc routing problem, namely Arc-MDP. This Arc-MDP model can be easily modified, applied to other arc routing problems, and solved by DRL methods.

- • Secondly, we present a novel data-driven method based on Deep Reinforcement Learning and Graph Attention to solve this problem effectively and efficiently. This model can generate solutions for an instance in much less time than heuristic and exact methods.

- • Last but not least, we introduce two metaheuristic methods inspired by nature evolution and swarm intelligence, namely the Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), as new metaheuristics for CPP-LC. We then conducted extensive experiments to compare our Arc-DRL with several heuristic baselines on various problem instances. The empirical results demonstrate the superior performance of our approaches over previous methods in both solution quality and evaluation time.
